Original synthetic fixtures generated for this project (MIT OR Apache-2.0).
Encoder and independent reference decoder: ImageMagick 7.1.2-34 Q16-HDRI.
No third-party artwork is included.

Generation commands:
magick -size 8x8 gradient:red-blue -alpha set -channel A -evaluate set 60% +channel -define dds:compression=dxt5 -define dds:mipmaps=0 gradient-bc3.dds
magick gradient-bc3.dds -depth 8 rgba:gradient-bc3.rgba
magick -size 8x8 gradient:yellow-green -define dds:compression=dxt1 -define dds:mipmaps=0 gradient-bc1.dds
magick gradient-bc1.dds -depth 8 rgba:gradient-bc1.rgba

RGB565 expansion/interpolation can differ by one integer channel value between
decoders. Tests require exact alpha and at most one unit RGB error.

rgba-mip-chain.dds: original 32x16 RGBA gradient generated by
examples/dds_mipmaps.rs, including six mip levels down to 1x1. MIT OR Apache-2.0.
ImageMagick identifies this file as DDS 32x16, 2860 bytes. The native Windows
editor 5.1.12 opened the same file on CASTOR on 2026-10-25 and displayed its
32x16 base surface without an import error. This checks base-level acceptance;
there is no claim of native mip-filter equivalence.

export-bc1.dds and export-bc3.dds: original 64x64 color/alpha grid, encoded by
examples/dds_compression.rs with a complete mip chain. Independent base-surface
reference bytes generated with FFmpeg 8.1.3:
ffmpeg -v error -i export-bc1.dds -f rawvideo -pix_fmt rgba export-bc1.rgba
ffmpeg -v error -i export-bc3.dds -f rawvideo -pix_fmt rgba export-bc3.rgba

Both exported files opened in the native Windows editor 5.1.12 on CASTOR
on 2026-10-25. export-bc3-native.rgba was captured via its clipboard PNG format
and converted to raw RGBA with ImageMagick. Compared with FFmpeg, native alpha
and visible RGB differ by at most one level (interpolation rounding). Hidden RGB
at zero alpha is not required to survive the native clipboard.

A second clipboard-PNG capture of the BC1 export preserved alpha exactly and
matched FFmpeg visible RGB within one level.

export-bc4.dds and export-bc5.dds use the same original grid and generator, with
DX10 BC4_UNORM/BC5_UNORM headers. FFmpeg 8.1.3 produced the corresponding .rgba references
using the commands above with bc4/bc5 substituted. Comparisons cover stored red
and red/green channels; decoder presentation of unstored channels can differ.
Data mipmaps average channel values directly and discard source transparency.
The explicit DX10 formats avoid legacy ATI2/3Dc channel-swizzle conventions.
FFmpeg legacy ATI2 handling is documented in its decoder source:
https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg/blob/master/libavcodec/dds.c

DX10 BC4 and BC5 exports also opened in the native Windows editor 5.1.12 on
2026-10-25. Its BC5 clipboard PNG retained red/green within one level of FFmpeg,
with blue zero and opaque alpha.

export-bc2.dds: original 64x64 color/alpha grid from
examples/dds_compression.rs, with BC2/DXT3 explicit 4-bit alpha and a complete
mip chain. MIT OR Apache-2.0. Independent reference export-bc2.rgba generated
on 2026-10-26 with FFmpeg 8.1.3:
ffmpeg -v error -i export-bc2.dds -f rawvideo -pix_fmt rgba export-bc2.rgba
Native Windows opening and clipboard comparison remain pending for BC2.
